threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: The riskiest row in the table. _meta.systemPrompt is confirmed only for claude-agent-acp, watched live. Whether codex-acp honours the same key is inference — and the research doc's own finding is that _meta semantics are explicitly not standardised, so agents are free to ignore keys they do not know. If codex-acp ignores it, pikamini on Codex has no identity, no ghost context and no skills, which is not a degraded agent but a different one.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: This signature is the least considered thing in the document. Passing emit as a callback mirrors the current StreamFunc, but a tool-calling loop is not one call — it is model → tools → model → tools, and Complete returning a single StopReason cannot express 'stopped to call a tool, resume me'. Either Complete returns a tool-call intent the loop acts on, or the loop lives inside Complete and the provider owns it, which defeats the abstraction. I would not implement from this shape as written.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: The Fake is the part of this I am most confident about and the part with the clearest payoff independent of everything else. Seventeen bridge test files exist and none can drive a turn, because a turn needs a subprocess. If phases 4 and 5 never happen, this alone changes how testable the bridge is — which is an argument for doing phase 3 first and deciding the rest afterwards.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: Models on Capabilities overlaps with ModelProvider.Models() in phase 5 and I am not sure both should exist. Capabilities answers 'what can this runtime do' at wiring time; ModelProvider answers 'what can I select' at call time. For the CLI runtime they are the same list. Possible answer: drop it from Capabilities and let callers ask the provider — but that assumes every runtime has a provider, which the CLI one does not. Genuinely unresolved.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: StreamFunc2 is a placeholder name and should not survive review. Naming a type after its predecessor's version number guarantees confusion in two months when nobody remembers which was which. Candidates: StreamHandler, EventSink, OnEvent. Worth deciding before phase 2 writes it into every signature.
